phase: CP.2 storage qualification; implementation not started

service_observation.limits: Read-only systemd/proc observation; secret environment values not read out or retained. No request, restart or configuration mutation.

findings.observation: add queues extraction; add_sync invokes extraction. Neither is a caller-exact governed declaration/observation commit with immutable Blaine provenance and scoped idempotency.
findings.limits: Source review and retained prior research; no new ingestion request sent.

findings.observation: Raw manager stores exact context plus JSON filter_tags with a caller-provided optional ID. create_with_redis commits and refreshes PostgreSQL before caching. These are useful substrate mechanisms, not proof of Blaine committed readback or atomic registry/retry semantics.
Public create_raw_memory selects an agent and supplies its state to create_raw_memory_manager. The request exposes no no-embedding or use_cache switch.
findings.inference: At default BUILD_EMBEDDINGS_FOR_MEMORY=true, exact submitted content is processed by the agent embedding configuration before storage. Current trusted CP.1 bindings do not grant this processing route. Post-read filtering cannot qualify that processing boundary.

findings.observation: Raw by-ID cache read checks scope and optional user; unlike SQL fallback it does not explicitly compare cached organization with actor.organization_id. Search passes organization, user, tags and read scopes. MIRIX scopes are not Blaine lineage/security/provenance.
findings.limits: No cross-tenant exploit attempted. A restricted adapter could narrow some methods; no all-method safe adapter is established.

findings.observation: Single globally keyed row ID; optional IDs/tags enable a possible future scoped encoding, but do not implement a scoped payload-digest compare-and-set/readback receipt. SQL uniqueness alone is not the required replay/conflict contract.
findings.limits: Does not prove scoped idempotency impossible; requires an approved adapter and response-loss tests before qualification.

findings.observation: Raw storage advertises a 14-day TTL. Cleanup selects by updated_at across the raw table with no Blaine retention/provenance partition.
findings.limits: No cleanup executed; no claim the nightly job is installed or that its synthetic actor succeeds. This is an unresolved lifecycle contract, not measured data loss.

findings.observation: Internal create accepts agent_state=None/use_cache=False, which could avoid those processing branches. It is not the existing Blaine HTTP seam and does not itself establish scoped registry atomicity, all-method isolation, retention or response-loss recovery.
findings.decision: Do not silently switch to internal ORM writes or a second database. Stop and request a reviewed existing-substrate adapter/server boundary before implementation.

decision: Existing public integration is NOT QUALIFIED for governed CP.2 writes. No alternate store, upstream change, host reconfiguration or protected write attempted. This is a STOP under the explicit storage/processing boundary conditions, not a claim that MIRIX/PostgreSQL is inherently incapable.
next_increment: Resume CP.2 storage qualification after reviewing the narrowly scoped MIRIX/approved-storage adapter boundary; not CP.3
